slides.title: What assistants get wrong in analysis
slides.text: Session 1 What assistants get wrong in analysis Name the five places where an assisted analysis goes wrong without an error List the assumptions in an assistant's code, line by line Test an assumption by changing it and reading how far the number moves 01

slides.title: The code ran. That is all you know
slides.text: The case The code ran. That is all you know Dareen, analystWhat is our on-time delivery rate? Rafiq, assistantYour on-time delivery rate is 85.3%. I joined deliveries to their delivery scans and averaged the on-time flag. 79.4% the rate under Hudhud's own written definition No error was raised Valid SQL, a number between 0 and 1, a confident sentence. Six points from the answer.

slides.title: An analysis goes wrong quietly in five places
slides.text: Where to look An analysis goes wrong quietly in five places Place The silent choice At Hudhud Definition What the measure means The on-time rule changed on 1 April 2026; the system flag follows whichever was in force Grain What one row is, after each join A scan can be uploaded twice; a route has several plan versions Filter Which rows left, and why Test shipments, cancelled orders, the last day of a period Denominator Out of what Delivered parcels, or every parcel that left a hub? Time Which clock, which calendar Scan times are UTC, promises are local: three hours apart

slides.title: One question, six numbers, 9.7 points apart
slides.text: Lab 1.1, measured One question, six numbers, 9.7 points apart D-1 all year, delivered only 89.2% The reply: flag, joined to scans 85.3% Flag, one row per parcel 83.9% Flag, tests removed 83.8% D-2 all year, delivered only 81.9% D-2 all year, dispatched 79.4% Every row runs. Each is "the on-time rate" under some reading. Only the last follows the written definition.

slides.title: The April jump is a change of ruler, not of deliveries
slides.text: The director's question, first look The April jump is a change of ruler, not of deliveries On-time rate March 2026 April 2026 Dashboard tile (system flag) 89.4% 80.0% D-2 applied to both months 79.9% 79.8% What changed on 1 April On time now means by the promised hour, and a parcel never delivered counts as late. What an assistant sees A column named on_time_flag. Nothing in its name says it holds two rules.

slides.title: Agents are weakest where analysis needs several steps and context
slides.text: Beyond one case Agents are weakest where analysis needs several steps and context 14.55% accuracy of the best agent on the hardest tasks of DABstep, over 450 multi-step data analysis tasks from a financial analytics platform BLADE, 12 research datasets Compared with expert analysts, language models were "often limited to basic analyses". What the hard tasks share Several steps, documentation that must be read, and one precise answer.

slides.title: Read the reply as a list of choices, not as an answer
slides.text: The method of Lab 1.1 Read the reply as a list of choices, not as an answer 1 · The measure Which column or expression is averaged or counted? → 2 · Each join What is one row before it, and after it? → 3 · Each filter Which rows left? Which should have left and stayed? → 4 · The pool Which periods and groups are folded into one number? Then test. Change one choice, rerun, read how far the number moves. A choice that moves it is an assumption worth stating.

slides.title: What do you know when the reply runs?
slides.text: Checkpoint What do you know when the reply runs? Rafiq returns a query for "share of parcels with a second delivery attempt". It runs without error and prints 0.11. What has been established? That 11% is about right, since the value is plausible That the query is valid SQL on these tables That the denominator is dispatched parcels That a second run would print 0.11 again

slides.title: Delegate, assist or keep
slides.text: Session 2 Delegate, assist or keep Distinguish delegating a step, being assisted on it and keeping it Sort the steps of an analysis plan with a reason for each Explain what unchecked delegation costs the analyst's own skill 02

slides.title: Every step of a plan is delegated, assisted or kept
slides.text: A vocabulary Every step of a plan is delegated, assisted or kept Delegate The assistant does the step. You check the result with a light check: a count, the axes, a diff. Profile the tables. Assist The assistant drafts. You do the part that decides the number, or you recompute it another way. The monthly on-time rate. Keep You do it. The assistant may criticise your draft; it does not decide. What "late" means this year.

slides.title: Three questions sort most steps
slides.text: A rule of thumb Three questions sort most steps Is judgement the product? A definition, a causal claim, a recommendation. Then keep. Is the result cheap to check? A count against the source, a chart you can read. Are the stakes high? Would a wrong result reach a decision before anyone noticed? def suggest(step): if step["judgement_is_the_product"]: return "keep" if step["cheap_to_check"] and not step["high_stakes"]: return "delegate" return "assist" The rule moves the judgement, it does not remove it. Someone still decides what is cheap to check and what is high stakes.

slides.title: Ten steps: three delegated, four assisted, three kept
slides.text: The late-delivery plan Ten steps: three delegated, four assisted, three kept # Step Mode # Step Mode 1 Decide what late means keep 6 Join route plans, long against short assist 2 Load and profile the tables delegate 7 Cause or coincidence in Dammam keep 3 Remove tests and duplicate scans assist 8 Summarise complaint categories assist 4 Monthly on-time rate assist 9 Tidy the notebook delegate 5 Chart from the checked table delegate 10 Recommend which city first keep

slides.title: Learners who delegated everything finished, and learned less
slides.text: Why "keep" exists Learners who delegated everything finished, and learned less 52 developers learning a new library, assigned at random to work with or without an assistant 17% lower score for the assisted group on a quiz of understanding, code reading and debugging 3 of 6 ways of using the assistant kept learning intact: the ones with cognitive engagement The skill that erodes is the one supervision needs. Reading code and finding what is wrong with it is exactly the work of Day 2.

slides.title: Feeling faster is not a measurement
slides.text: Your own sense of it Feeling faster is not a measurement Forecast before the tasks 24% faster Belief after the tasks 20% faster Measured 19% slower Sixteen experienced open-source developers, 246 tasks in their own projects, each task assigned at random to allow or forbid AI tools (early 2025).

slides.title: Confidence in the tool goes with less checking
slides.text: Who checks, and who does not Confidence in the tool goes with less checking Higher confidence in the assistant went with less critical thinking about its output. Higher confidence in one's own skill went with more critical thinking about its output. A survey of 319 knowledge workers who described 936 real uses of generative AI at work. The habit this course builds. The check is decided before the run, in the brief, so it does not depend on how confident you feel afterwards.

slides.title: On a kept step the assistant argues; you decide
slides.text: Using the assistant on a kept step On a kept step the assistant argues; you decide YouI will apply D-2 to the whole year. Give me the three strongest objections a board member could raise. Assistant1. The dashboard showed D-1 numbers for six months. 2. Staff were measured on D-1 then. 3. D-2 needs the promised hour, which older exports may lack. Ask for objections , missing cases, a second reading. Do not ask "which definition should I use?" The decision and its reason are written by you, in your words. If you cannot defend it without the assistant, it was not kept.

Counting complaints and parcels per service Drawing a bar chart of the two rates Drafting the query for complaints per 1,000 parcels Deciding whether complaints are counted per parcel or per customer

slides.title: The delegation brief
slides.text: Session 3 The delegation brief Write the five parts of a delegation brief Write acceptance checks that a reviewer can apply without asking the author Turn a failed check into a precise follow-up request 03

slides.title: A brief has five parts, written before the assistant runs
slides.text: The delegation brief A brief has five parts, written before the assistant runs For Tahani Al-Qasim: the monthly on-time rate, October 2025 to September 2026, as a table and one chart. Use deliveries (one row per parcel) and customers. Month is the month of created_at. Do not join scans. On time is D-2 for every month: delivered_at at or before promised_by; a dispatched parcel never delivered is late. One query per step. No test shipments, no cancelled orders. Stop after each step and show its row count. Twelve rows, 2025-10 to 2026-09. Deliveries sum to the dispatched, non-test parcels. No month moves more than 5 points. QuestionDataDefinitionsConstraintsAcceptance checks

slides.title: An acceptance check names a number, a count or a condition
slides.text: The fifth part An acceptance check names a number, a count or a condition A wish A check a reviewer can apply The numbers should look reasonable Every rate is between 0 and 1; no month differs from the one before by more than 5 points Make sure nothing is double counted The working table has one row per delivery_id Cover the whole year Exactly 12 rows, 2025-10 to 2026-09 Use the right parcels Deliveries sum to the dispatched, non-test parcels, counted by me The test of a check. Could a colleague apply it to the output without asking you a question?

slides.title: The expected value comes from your query, never from the reply
slides.text: Independence The expected value comes from your query, never from the reply def check_total(result): expected = U.one(con, """ SELECT COUNT(*) FROM deliveries d JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = d.customer_id WHERE c.segment <> 'TEST' AND d.status <> 'cancelled'""") got = int(result["deliveries"].sum()) return got == expected, (got, expected) A check that cannot fail "Ask the assistant to confirm its total" compares the answer with itself. Small, and yours Five lines of SQL you wrote and understand are worth more than fifty you read.

slides.title: Small steps with a stop after each find errors while they are small
slides.text: Constraints that pay Small steps with a stop after each find errors while they are small Step 1 · Working table stop: rows, tests removed, cancelled removed → Step 2 · Monthly rate stop: 12 rows, the total, the range → Step 3 · Chart stop: axis from zero, rates not counts Stepwise An error is found one step after it is made, with one query to read. All at once An agent that runs ten steps hands you ten steps of code and one number.

slides.title: The first reply said the right words and failed one check
slides.text: Lab 1.3, measured The first reply said the right words and failed one check Check First reply After one follow-up Total equals dispatched parcels 496,046 against 486,078 486,078 Twelve months pass pass Rates in range, no 5-point jump pass pass Yearly on-time rate 77.8% 79.4% Its sentence was correct. "Under D-2, without test shipments." The 9,968 cancelled orders in the denominator were visible only to the check.

slides.title: A follow-up names the check, the number it saw and the rule
slides.text: When a check fails A follow-up names the check, the number it saw and the rule VagueThis looks too low. Are you sure? Please double-check everything. AssistantYou are right to question it. I have reviewed the query and it is correct. The rate is 77.8%. PreciseCheck 1 failed: the deliveries add up to more than the dispatched parcels. Cancelled orders are in no rate. Fix step 2. AssistantI had left cancelled orders in the denominator. They are removed; the total equals the dispatched parcels.

slides.title: Which line is an acceptance check?
slides.text: Checkpoint Which line is an acceptance check? A brief asks for late deliveries per city for the year. Which line can Yasser apply to the result without asking the author anything? Four rows, one per city, and the late counts sum to my own count of late dispatched parcels Be careful not to double count parcels with several scans Use one query per step and stop after each step Have the assistant confirm that its totals are correct

slides.title: Context files for a project
slides.text: Session 4 Context files for a project Decide what belongs in a project context file and what belongs in a brief Write the definitions, checks and prohibitions of an analysis project as rules Compare two runs of one brief on code, numbers and checks 04

slides.title: A context file tells every request what the project already knows
slides.text: Project context A context file tells every request what the project already knows A plain text file in the project that the assistant reads before every request. One open convention is AGENTS.md: "a README for agents". Written for software projects: build steps, tests, code style. An analysis project needs different sections. Section For an analysis project Data Tables, what one row is, what the assistant may see Definitions Measures, denominators, exclusions, time Conventions Engine, style, what a result looks like Checks What to run and show before answering Do not Joins and outputs that are never right here

slides.title: The file holds what is true for every request; the brief holds this one
slides.text: What goes where The file holds what is true for every request; the brief holds this one In the context file On time is D-2 for every month Cancelled orders and test shipments are in no rate Scan times are UTC Never join scans to count parcels In the brief Tahani's question and her deadline The steps of this task The acceptance checks of this result What to stop and show Neither holds rows or secrets. A context file is sent with every request, to whatever model is configured.

slides.title: Write rules a reply can be held to, not explanations
slides.text: How to write it Write rules a reply can be held to, not explanations ## Definitions - On time is D-2 for every month: delivered_at <= promised_by. - A dispatched parcel never delivered is late. - Never use on_time_flag across months. - Denominator: dispatched parcels (delivered, failed or returned). - A parcel belongs to the month of created_at. ## Do not - Do not join scans to count parcels. One fact per line, in the words of the columns. Each line can be checked against a reply. Short: long files are followed less well and cost tokens on every request. It has an owner and a date, like any definition.

slides.title: One short brief, with and without the file
slides.text: Lab 1.4, measured One short brief, with and without the file "Monthly on-time rate for Tahani, whole year." Yearly rate Off by Checks passed Without the context file 86.7% 7.3 points 2 of 3 With the context file 81.9% 2.5 points 2 of 3 Written definition, recomputed 79.4% 0 3 of 3 Without UTC scan times against local promises, test shipments kept, a join to scans. With All of that fixed. One rule of the file ignored: delivered parcels only.

slides.title: A context file lowers the number of errors. It finds none
slides.text: The limit A context file lowers the number of errors. It finds none What it did Three of four errors did not happen. That is real, and cheap. What it cannot do Tell you whether a given reply followed it. The file stated the denominator rule; the reply broke it. Close the loop. Every error that verification finds becomes a line in the file, or a check in the brief, or both. The file is the project's memory of its own mistakes.

slides.title: What does the context file change?
slides.text: Checkpoint What does the context file change? Your project's context file states the on-time definition and the denominator. A reply arrives that says it followed both. What do you do with the reply's number? Report it, since the file was in place and the reply cites it Add a stricter line to the file, then report the number Apply the acceptance checks to it, exactly as without the file Discard it and write the query yourself from the start

slides.title: A project context file
slides.text: Lab 1.4 · 25 min A project context file Add a project context file, rerun a brief and compare the outputs on code, numbers and acceptance checks. D1_4_context_file.ipynb Read the starting context file and find its gaps 4 min Write the three missing sections 8 min Rerun the brief without and with the file; compare 9 min Write the verification note 4 min ✱ Stretch: Add the check the remaining error would fail by name

slides.title: Decide before the run what you hand over and how you will know
slides.text: Day 1 recap Decide before the run what you hand over and how you will know Read for choices A reply that runs has proved its syntax. The measure, the grain, the filters and the denominator are choices to list and test. Delegate, assist, keep Sort steps by whether you can check them cheaply, whether judgement is the product and what is at stake. Brief and context State definitions and acceptance checks first. A context file lowers errors; only a check on the output finds them.

slides.title: Verify
slides.text: Today Verify Session 1 · Recompute it another way A number is verified when a second, independent path reaches it, and every point of the gap has a named cause Session 2 · Joins, filters and denominators Most wrong numbers in assisted SQL come from rows that were multiplied, rows that were dropped, and a denominator nobody stated Session 3 · Charts and words A chart is a set of encodings and a summary is a list of claims: each one is checked against a query Session 4 · Ask it twice The same request gives different code and different numbers on different runs: only conclusions that hold in every run are reported as found

slides.title: What was missing from the one-line request?
slides.text: Review · Day 1 What was missing from the one-line request? "What is our on-time delivery rate?" returned 85.3%; the written definition gives 79.4%. Which part of a brief would have prevented most of the gap? A longer statement of the question Constraints on the engine and the number of queries A more capable model The definitions: which on-time rule, and out of which parcels

slides.title: Recompute it another way
slides.text: Session 1 Recompute it another way Choose a recomputation path that shares as little as possible with the first Recompute a headline rate in SQL without an assistant Reconcile two numbers by applying one difference at a time 01

slides.title: Two analyses of one city tell two stories
slides.text: Dammam, by quarter Two analyses of one city tell two stories On-time rate, Dammam 2025 Q4 2026 Q1 2026 Q2 2026 Q3 The story Rafiq, in pandas 86.9% 87.1% 87.1% 84.3% "Steady, a dip of under three points" You, in SQL from the definitions 79.6% 80.0% 79.7% 72.3% A fall of 7.4 points Two numbers that differ are not yet a finding. One of them is wrong, or both are. Until the gap is explained you do not know which.

slides.title: A second path verifies only what it does not share with the first
slides.text: Recompute another way A second path verifies only what it does not share with the first Independent Starts from the written definitions Starts from the base table, one row per parcel Written by you, before reading the first path's code closely Not independent The same query, translated to another engine The same joined table, aggregated differently The assistant asked to "double-check" its own answer Share the question and the data. Share nothing else.

slides.title: Five ways to reach the same number differently
slides.text: Choosing the second path Five ways to reach the same number differently Another… How Catches Starting table From deliveries only, no scans Fan-outs, dropped rows Grain Daily counts first, then sum to the quarter Period boundaries, averaging of averages Engine SQL if the first was pandas, or the reverse Type and time handling, silent NULL rules Source A total from finance or the operations system Missing or duplicated data upstream Sample by hand Twenty parcels, judged against the definition by eye A definition coded wrongly in both paths

slides.title: Reconcile the gap one cause per row, until nothing is left
slides.text: Lab 2.1, measured Reconcile the gap one cause per row, until nothing is left Dammam, third quarter of 2026 On-time rate Change Rafiq's method 84.28% + compare in local time, not UTC 74.73% −9.54 + quarter of created_at, not of the scan 74.78% +0.04 + every dispatched parcel, undelivered ones late 72.46% −2.31 + no test shipments 72.26% −0.21 Your SQL 72.26% 0 left Change one choice per row. The first row reproduces their number; the last equals yours. The changes add up to the whole gap: 12.0 points. A remainder means an error nobody has found yet, possibly yours.

slides.title: One time-zone error hid the one thing the director needed
slides.text: Why it mattered here One time-zone error hid the one thing the director needed −7.4 points Dammam's on-time rate from the second to the third quarter of 2026, under D-2 −2.8 points the same change in the assisted analysis The mechanism A UTC scan time compared with a local promise makes every parcel delivered up to three hours after the cut-off look on time. The coincidence Dammam's new problem is evening deliveries, just after the cut-off: exactly the parcels the error hides.

slides.title: The first recomputation is done without the assistant
slides.text: The course's AI policy The first recomputation is done without the assistant Independence A second query from the same assistant shares its reading of the columns and its habits. Skill Reading code and finding what is wrong with it is the skill that erodes when it is never exercised. Accountability In the defence you recompute one headline number live, with no assistant. Practise here. After the first recomputation the assistant is welcome: to explain a gap you have measured, or to write the tedious rows of a bridge you designed.

slides.title: Which recomputation is independent?
slides.text: Checkpoint Which recomputation is independent? An assistant reports 3.1 failed parcels per 100 dispatched in Jeddah, from a query that joins deliveries to scans. Which second path tells you most? Rewriting the same query in pandas and comparing Asking the assistant to review its query for mistakes Counting failed and dispatched parcels from deliveries alone, by status Running the same query for Riyadh and checking it is similar

slides.title: Joins, filters and denominators
slides.text: Session 2 Joins, filters and denominators Count rows before and after each join to find a fan-out Find the rows a filter dropped with an anti-join State the denominator of a rate in one sentence and test the code against it 02

slides.title: You can write a safe join. Today you audit one you did not write
slides.text: What you already know You can write a safe join. Today you audit one you did not write From SQL and Data Wrangling (FN-104) Grain, keys and cardinality Filters and NULL Joins that do not double count Testing queries What changes with an assistant The query arrives complete and fluent You did not make its choices, so you do not remember them It joins tables you would have left out Its sentence describes the intent, not the code

slides.title: Count rows and distinct keys after every join
slides.text: Check 1 · Lab 2.2, measured Count rows and distinct keys after every join Stage of the assisted query Rows Distinct parcels Reading deliveries, with its filters 21,158 21,158 One row is one parcel + join route_plans 22,699 21,158 1,541 extra rows: plan versions + left join driver_shifts 23,778 21,158 More rows: split shifts + AND s.hours >= 8 21,620 20,164 994 parcels gone The fastest check in analysis. If rows and distinct keys differ, one parcel has become several rows, and every average after it is weighted wrongly.

slides.title: Several rows per key, and the join took them all
slides.text: Two fan-outs, one cause Several rows per key, and the join took them all WITH plan AS ( SELECT * FROM route_plans QUALIFY version = MAX(version) OVER ( PARTITION BY hub_id, plan_date, route_id) ) FROM scope s JOIN plan p ON p.hub_id = s.hub_id AND p.plan_date = s.route_date AND p.route_id = s.route_id route_plans One row per version. A route replanned at midday has two or three. driver_shifts One row per shift. A driver on a split shift has two that day. The question to ask of every join What is one row of the table on the right, and is the join key unique in it?

slides.title: A condition on the right table turns a left join into an inner join
slides.text: A filter in the wrong place A condition on the right table turns a left join into an inner join LEFT JOIN driver_shifts s ON s.driver_id = d.driver_id AND s.shift_date = d.route_date WHERE d.city = 'Dammam' AND d.status = 'delivered' AND s.hours >= 8 What it did Removed every parcel whose driver had no single shift of eight hours: 994 parcels on split-shift days. What nobody asked The reply said "kept full shifts". The request never mentioned shifts.

slides.title: An anti-join against the scope names every missing row
slides.text: Check 2 · Lab 2.2, measured An anti-join against the scope names every missing row WITH scope AS (...), -- from the sentence j AS (SELECT DISTINCT delivery_id FROM (...)) -- their joined rows SELECT reason, COUNT(*) AS parcels FROM scope LEFT JOIN j ON j.delivery_id = scope.delivery_id WHERE j.delivery_id IS NULL GROUP BY reason Missing from the assisted result Parcels Driver on a split shift 994 Never delivered: failed or returned 688 Created on the last day 236 Of 22,082 in scope 1,918

slides.title: Say the denominator as a sentence, then test the code against it
slides.text: Check 3 Say the denominator as a sentence, then test the code against it The sentence Dispatched Dammam parcels created in the three months, each counted once, classified by the plan in force on its route and day. Words of the sentence What the code must show dispatched delivered, failed and returned; not cancelled created in the three months from 1 July up to, not including, 1 October each counted once rows equal distinct parcels the plan in force the highest version only If you cannot say it in one sentence, the rate has no meaning yet. The sentence also goes into the report, under the number.

slides.title: The conclusion survived. The numbers did not
slides.text: After the repair The conclusion survived. The numbers did not Dammam, July to September 2026 Short routes Long routes Gap Counted Assisted query, four errors 81.4% 70.3% 11.1 points 21,620 rows Corrected 79.0% 68.1% 11.0 points 22,082 parcels What to say Parcels on routes above 60 planned stops are on time 11 points less often: 68.1% against 79.0%. What not to say "The direction was right." A report quotes rates, and both were over two points too high.

slides.title: Which check finds it first?
slides.text: Checkpoint Which check finds it first? An assisted query joins complaints to deliveries to scans and reports "complaints per late parcel". You suspect a fan-out. What do you run first? Rows against distinct complaint ids after each join The final total, compared with last month's report An anti-join of complaints against the result A careful read of the join conditions

slides.title: Charts and words
slides.text: Session 3 Charts and words Read a chart's axis, measure and time window against the table behind it Split a written summary into claims and test each with a query Check that a summary does not misstate one city or language group 03

slides.title: Three encodings decide what a chart says
slides.text: Reading a chart you did not draw Three encodings decide what a chart says The measure What is on the y axis: a count or a rate? Of what, out of what? The axis Where does it start? Is the scale the same for every series? The window Which periods are shown, and is each one complete? Read the code, not the picture. An assistant's chart comes with the table and the plot call that made it: the encodings are written there.

slides.title: Same parcels, same weeks, opposite message
slides.text: Lab 2.3, drawn from the lab's run Same parcels, same weeks, opposite message The assistant's chart: counts, an axis from 300, two partial weeks. Redrawn: rates, an axis from 0, complete weeks.

slides.title: By count Riyadh is the problem. By rate it is Dammam
slides.text: The measure By count Riyadh is the problem. By rate it is Dammam Complete weeks since July Riyadh Dammam Late parcels per week 847 464 Share of dispatched parcels late 20.3% 27.7% Tahani asked which city to fix first. A count answers "where are most of the late parcels?" A rate answers "where is the service worst?" Both are legitimate. The chart must say which it shows, and the title must not claim the other.

slides.title: A summary is a list of claims, and each claim has a query
slides.text: Words · Lab 2.3, measured A summary is a list of claims, and each claim has a query The assistant's sentence Verdict All 20,000 complaints say Damaged parcels are the most common complaint, about half fails Late is first at 36%; damaged is 23% Most complaints are written in English fails 56% are in Arabic Madinah has the fewest complaints, so it needs the least attention fails Fewest by count, most per 1,000 parcels: 60.3 Late-delivery complaints from Dammam rose after June holds From 94 to 144 a month Arabic and English complaints raise the same issues fails Late is 40% of Arabic complaints, 32% of English

slides.title: The summary was written from the first 500 rows
slides.text: Read the code before the words The summary was written from the first 500 rows sample = con.sql(""" SELECT city, language, category, text FROM complaints LIMIT 500 """).df() The export is sorted by channel, email first. English, first 500 92% English, all complaints 44% Damaged, first 500 51% Damaged, all complaints 23% A model cannot read 20,000 texts in one request, so something chose which ones it read. Find out what.

slides.title: The sample left out a city and a language
slides.text: Responsible use The sample left out a city and a language Madinah Fewest complaints by count: 3,239. Most per 1,000 parcels: 60.3, against 38 to 40 in the other three cities. The summary: "needs the least attention". Customers who write in Arabic 56% of all complaints. Late delivery is 40% of what they raise, against 32% for English. The summary: "the same issues in the same proportions". A check for every summary. Break the claim down by city and by language before it leaves your notebook. A group missing from the sample is a group the summary speaks for without having heard.

slides.title: Which sentence needs a different query?
slides.text: Checkpoint Which sentence needs a different query? An assistant writes: "Refund complaints are rare in Jeddah (742 of 5,573), so cash on delivery works well there." What do you check? That 742 of 5,573 is the right count for Jeddah The count, and refund complaints per 1,000 cash-on-delivery parcels by city A further 500 complaint texts from Jeddah, read by the assistant The share of refunds among Jeddah's complaints against other cities

slides.title: A chart and a summary against the data
slides.text: Lab 2.3 · 25 min A chart and a summary against the data Check an assistant's chart and complaint summary against the data, claim by claim. D2_3_charts_and_words.ipynb Recompute the charted series and read its encodings 8 min Redraw the chart from the checked table 4 min Test each sentence of the complaint summary 9 min Write the verification note 4 min ✱ Stretch: Compute complaints per 1,000 parcels by city and language

slides.title: Ask it twice
slides.text: Session 4 Ask it twice Explain why one request yields different analyses between runs Tabulate the analytic choices, numbers and conclusions of repeated runs Separate the conclusions that held in every run from those that did not 04

slides.title: One request, one context file, the same settings, five answers
slides.text: Lab 2.4, measured One request, one context file, the same settings, five answers Run What it measured Worst city Dammam since July Cities "worse" Code like run 1 1 D-2, dispatched parcels Dammam 72.3% 1 1.00 2 D-2, delivered parcels Dammam 74.6% 1 0.82 3 Late parcels per month Riyadh 2,042 a month 4 0.37 4 The system flag Dammam 72.3% 4 0.73 5 D-2, against April to June only Dammam 72.3% 1 0.73 If you had asked once, you would hold one of these five and would not know which.

slides.title: Runs differ because the model samples and the request leaves room
slides.text: Sources of variation Runs differ because the model samples and the request leaves room Sampling Each word is drawn from a distribution. Temperature widens or narrows it; few hosted models promise identical output even at zero. Room in the request "Worst" and "got worse" each allow several measures and baselines. The model picks one per run. A moving service A hosted model can be updated behind the same name. Next month's run is another run. You control the middle one. A brief that fixes the measure and the baseline removes most of the spread in the table.

slides.title: Twenty-nine teams, one data set, one question
slides.text: Not only models Twenty-nine teams, one data set, one question 0.89 to 2.93 range of the estimated effect, as odds ratios, across the teams 20 and 9 teams that found a significant effect, and teams that did not 21 different combinations of covariates among 29 analyses The difference with an assistant. A human analyst makes one set of choices and can be asked why. The assistant makes a new set on every run, silently.

slides.title: Report as found only what held in every run
slides.text: The variability table Report as found only what held in every run Dammam got worse 5 of 5 Dammam is the worst city since July 4 of 5 No other city got worse 3 of 5 Held in every run Robust to the choices the assistant varies. Still to be verified once. Held in some Depends on a choice. Find the choice before the conclusion goes anywhere.

slides.title: Three of five is not "60% true"
slides.text: Reading the disagreement Three of five is not "60% true" Run Why it departed Under the definitions 3 Counted late parcels per month A growing company has more of everything 4 Averaged the system flag Two definitions before and after April A choice is right or wrong under the definitions. It is not outvoted. Both departing runs broke a rule the context file states. Variability told you where to look. The definitions told you who was right. Then verify the run you keep, as in Lab 2.1.

slides.title: Five identical answers can be identically wrong
slides.text: The limit Five identical answers can be identically wrong What repetition shows How much the answer depends on the model's own variation. What it cannot show An error every run shares: a column all five misread, a rule none was told. Record what was repeated The request and the context file, word for word The model's name and version Temperature, and a seed where the service supports one The number of runs, and all of them, not the best one

slides.title: Five runs agree. What do you know?
slides.text: Checkpoint Five runs agree. What do you know? You send one request five times with the same settings. All five replies report 31.2% of Madinah's complaints about late delivery. What has been established? That 31.2% is correct, since five independent runs agree That any later run of the request will also give 31.2% That the number does not depend on this model's run-to-run variation That the five replies used the same code

slides.title: Five runs of one request
slides.text: Lab 2.4 · 25 min Five runs of one request Repeat one request five times; tabulate differences in code, numbers and conclusions. D2_4_ask_it_twice.ipynb Run five replies to one fixed request 5 min Tabulate choices, code and numbers per run 8 min Decide which conclusions held in every run 8 min Write the verification note 4 min ✱ Stretch: Run the request five times live at temperature 0 and compare

slides.title: A number is yours when a second path reaches it and the gap is explained
slides.text: Day 2 recap A number is yours when a second path reaches it and the gap is explained Recompute from the definitions and the base table, without the assistant, then reconcile one cause per row. Count rows and distinct keys after each join; anti-join the scope; say the denominator. Charts: the measure, the axis, the window. Summaries: one query per claim, by city and by language. Ask five times: report what held in every run, and trace what did not to a choice. What Tahani can now be told. The April jump was the definition. Dammam fell 7.4 points from July, on long routes. Whether the optimiser caused it is yours to judge.

slides.title: Reproduce and disclose
slides.text: Today Reproduce and disclose Session 1 · Which data may go where The classification level of a table and the organisation's assistant policy decide its destination: hosted, local or neither Session 2 · Logging assisted work A rerun needs the prompt, the context, the model and its settings, the code, a fingerprint of the data and the output Session 3 · The peer rerun A package is reproducible when a peer reaches the same headline numbers from its logs alone, and every reported number has a logged step Session 4 · Disclosing assistance A report says which steps were assisted, by what, on which data, how they were verified and who answers for the numbers

slides.title: Which check finds which error?
slides.text: Review · Day 2 Which check finds which error? An assisted query reports 91% on time for Madinah in September. Its last line filters created_at BETWEEN '2026-09-01' AND '2026-09-30'. Which check shows what that filter did? An anti-join of the September scope against the query's rows Rows against distinct parcels after each join Running the request five times and comparing Reading the y axis of the chart

slides.title: Which data may go where
slides.text: Session 1 Which data may go where Classify the tables of an analysis by their most sensitive column Assign each table to a hosted assistant, a local assistant or neither under a written policy Enforce the assignment with a guard that runs before any prompt leaves 01

slides.title: The level decides the destination. Today the unit is a table of your analysis
slides.text: What you already know The level decides the destination. Today the unit is a table of your analysis From Responsible Data and AI Practice (FN-106) Four national levels: Top Secret, Secret, Restricted, Public The level follows the impact of unauthorised disclosure Generative AI tools: data classified Public only Three destinations: a hosted service, a model you run, or no model What an analysis adds Eight tables, joined, each with its own owner An assistant that reads whatever the notebook hands it Results, samples and error messages that travel back into prompts Aggregates you create, which need a level too

slides.title: A table takes the level of its most sensitive column
slides.text: Rules P-1 and P-2 of Hudhud's policy A table takes the level of its most sensitive column Column of deliveries Kind delivery_id, status, created_at … operational cod_amount commercial district location of a person recipient_phone contact The table Restricted, personal data Sixteen operational columns do not dilute two personal ones. A commercial column also makes a table Restricted: a contract rate, a route plan. A table nobody has classified is treated as Restricted. The data owner classifies. The analyst applies and records.

slides.title: Ten items, three destinations
slides.text: Lab 3.1, the reference result Ten items, three destinations Item Level Personal Rows may go to Item Level Personal Rows may go to hubs Public no hosted deliveries Restricted yes local customers Restricted yes local scans Restricted yes local drivers Restricted yes neither complaints Restricted yes local driver_shifts Restricted yes local on-time by city and month Public no hosted route_plans Restricted no local complaints by district Restricted yes local The course's main table is Restricted. Every request you sent in two days was about deliveries. The next slide says why that was allowed.

slides.title: The assistant wrote code about data it never saw
slides.text: Rule P-5 The assistant wrote code about data it never saw What left the notebook in every lab The request The context file Table and column names with their types What sends rows without your noticing "Here are the first five rows, what is wrong?" An error message that quotes a value An example in the context file An agent allowed to run queries and read their output An agent with a database connection reads rows by design. For Restricted tables that agent is local, or it does not get the connection.

slides.title: An aggregate is not safe because it is an aggregate
slides.text: Rule P-3 An aggregate is not safe because it is an aggregate On-time rate by city and month No personal column. Smallest cell: 3,200 parcels. Public , once its owner says so. May go to the hosted assistant. Complaints by district and category A district is where a person lives. Smallest cell: 4 complaints. Restricted. Four complaints about one driver in one district describe people. Two tests before an aggregate leaves: no column that locates or describes a person, and no cell built from fewer than 20 parcels. Then the owner classifies it.

slides.title: A third of the complaint texts carry a phone number
slides.text: Lab 3.1, measured A third of the complaint texts carry a phone number 31.5% of 20,000 complaint texts contain a mobile number: about 6,300 texts 155 of them in the 500 texts that the summary of Lab 2.3 read A pattern finds numbers. No pattern lists every name. Masking lowers the harm of a leak. It does not change the table's level. Texts written by customers stay on a local assistant, or are read by people. The labels in category can be counted without reading a text.

slides.title: A guard runs before every request, on good days and bad
slides.text: From document to code A guard runs before every request, on good days and bad def guard(tables, to, what): if what == "schema": return True # P-5 for t in tables: if DEST[t] == "neither": raise PermissionError(f"P-7: {t}") if to == "hosted" and DEST[t] != "hosted": raise PermissionError(f"P-4: {t}") return True Request Result Schema of deliveries, to hosted allowed Rows of hubs, to hosted allowed Rows of complaints, to hosted blocked, P-4 Rows of complaints, to local allowed Rows of drivers, to local blocked, P-7

slides.title: What may the hosted assistant receive?
slides.text: Checkpoint What may the hosted assistant receive? You want a hosted assistant to help explain why split-shift drivers have more failed deliveries. Under Hudhud's policy, what may you send it? Rows of driver_shifts, since driver_id is not a name Twenty sample rows of deliveries joined to shifts The drivers table with names masked The schema of both tables, and an aggregate its owner classified Public

slides.title: Hosted, local or neither
slides.text: Lab 3.1 · 25 min Hosted, local or neither Decide which tables a local or a hosted assistant may process, prove one decision on the data and enforce all of them in code. D3_1_which_data_where.ipynb Read the assistant policy and the table catalogue 5 min Classify each table and choose its destination 8 min Find the personal data in the complaint texts 4 min Write the guard and test it 4 min Write the verification note 4 min ✱ Stretch: Build an aggregate of complaints that may go to the hosted assistant

slides.title: Logging assisted work
slides.text: Session 2 Logging assisted work List what a log record must hold for a step to be rerun Write a log record with a data fingerprint for one assisted step Find what an incomplete log lacks before someone else has to 02

slides.title: A rerun needs nine things from every assisted step
slides.text: The run log A rerun needs nine things from every assisted step Field Why a peer needs it Field Why a peer needs it step To match it to a number in the report code The thing that is rerun request Word for word: what was asked data A fingerprint: was it this data? context A hash of the context file in force headline What the step produced then model Name and version: services change verified by The check, or its absence settings Temperature, a seed if supported Logged by the notebook, not typed afterwards. A log written from memory is a story about a log.

slides.title: Each line made sense on the day it was written
slides.text: Lab 3.2, the supplied log Each line made sense on the day it was written Step What the log says What a rerun lacks monthly_rate A request, a query, "the notebook assistant" Settings, context, data fingerprint, any check by_city The request is "same but by city" The code, context, data fingerprint; verified by "looked right" chart The code is "see notebook cell 14" The request, the context, the temperature, the data, the headline, any check "Same but by city" is a request only inside one conversation. A log line must stand without the lines around it.

slides.title: A fingerprint identifies the data without storing it
slides.text: Was it this data? A fingerprint identifies the data without storing it def fingerprint(table): row = con.sql(""" SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(delivery_id), CAST(MIN(created_at) AS VARCHAR), CAST(MAX(created_at) AS VARCHAR) FROM deliveries""").fetchall()[0] return {"rows": int(row[0]), "sha": U.sha([str(x) for x in row])} The peer's rerun gives Fingerprint So The same number same Reproduced Another number same The code or the environment differs Another number different The data changed: late corrections, a new export The same number different Luck. Look again

slides.title: One line per step, complete on its own
slides.text: Lab 3.2, the record you write One line per step, complete on its own {"step": "monthly_rate", "request": "Follow the brief below. Do step 2: the monthly on-time rate.", "context_sha": "a699f7c0c555", "model": "google/gemma-4-31b-it:free", "settings": {"temperature": 0.7}, "code": "result = con.sql(\"\"\"SELECT strftime(d.created_at, '%Y-%m') AS month, ...", "data": {"deliveries": {"rows": 500000, "sha": "..."}, "customers": {"rows": 3005, "sha": "..."}}, "headline": {"on_time_rate": 0.7942}, "verified_by": "three acceptance checks passed (3 of 3): total, months, rates"}

slides.title: Prove the log by rerunning from the line alone
slides.text: The test of a log Prove the log by rerunning from the line alone 1 · Read the line back from the file, not from memory → 2 · Run its code in a fresh connection → 3 · Compare headlines 0.7942 and 0.7942 → 4 · Compare fingerprints the data is the data You are your own first peer. If you cannot rerun your step from its log line today, nobody will next month.

slides.title: A log must be safe to publish
slides.text: The log leaves with the package A log must be safe to publish In the log Requests and replies, as sent Code Fingerprints and headline numbers What was sent: "schema only" Never in the log Rows or example values of Restricted data Keys and tokens A transcript in which a row was pasted Outputs that print personal data The capstone repository is public. Its transcripts are the evidence of how you worked, and of what the assistant was shown.

slides.title: What does this log line lack?
slides.text: Checkpoint What does this log line lack? A log line holds the step name, the full request, the model, temperature 0.2, the code and the headline number. A peer reruns the code and gets a different number. What can the peer not decide? Whether the model's settings were the same Whether the data changed or the computation did Whether the request was the one the report describes Whether the right code was rerun

slides.title: A run log
slides.text: Lab 3.2 · 25 min A run log Log prompts, model settings and outputs for one analysis, with a fingerprint of the data it ran on. D3_2_run_log.ipynb Read an incomplete log and list what a rerun lacks 5 min Write the log record and the data fingerprint 9 min Run one analysis through the logger and check the log 7 min Write the verification note 4 min ✱ Stretch: Change one row of a table and show that the fingerprint changes

slides.title: The peer rerun
slides.text: Session 3 The peer rerun Rerun a package from its log without asking its author Classify each headline number as matched, drifted or without a step Write a rerun log that an assessor can read in two minutes 03

slides.title: Reproduced: a peer reaches the headline numbers from the package alone
slides.text: A definition Reproduced: a peer reaches the headline numbers from the package alone A peer Someone who did not do the work and does not share your notebook's memory. The headline numbers The ones in the README and the report: what a reader will quote. From the package alone The log, the code and the data. No question to the author, no "run cell 14 first". Reproduced is not correct. A rerun shows that the numbers come from the logged steps. The verification notes are what argue that the steps are right.

slides.title: The package of an assisted analysis
slides.text: What is in the repository The package of an assisted analysis File Holds From README.md The question, the headline numbers, the method and disclosure paragraph Today brief.md, AGENTS.md What was delegated and under which rules Day 1 run_log.jsonl, transcripts/ Every assisted step, and the conversations as they happened Today headline.json Each headline number with the step and key it comes from Today notes.md, variability.md A verification note per headline number; five runs of one request Day 2 data_handling.md Each table's level and destination Today rerun_log.md Written by the peer, not by you Today

slides.title: Every headline number ends in one of three states
slides.text: Tracing Every headline number ends in one of three states Matched A logged step produces it, and the rerun gives the same value. Drifted A logged step claims to produce it, and the rerun gives another value. The text and the code have parted. No step Nothing in the log produces it. It was typed, copied or computed somewhere else. Trace from the report backwards. Start from each number a reader will quote and ask which line of the log made it.

slides.title: Three steps rerun. Two of four numbers are reproduced
slides.text: Lab 3.3, measured Three steps rerun. Two of four numbers are reproduced Headline number in the README Claimed Rerun Status Dammam on-time rate, third quarter of 2026 72.26% 72.26% matched Dammam on-time rate, second quarter of 2026 79.67% 79.67% matched On-time rate on long routes, July to September 68.41% 68.05% drifted Late complaints from Dammam per month since July 144 no step All three logged steps reran to their logged headline, on data with matching fingerprints. The package is still not reproduced: readers quote the README.

slides.title: The number with no step is probably right. It still fails
slides.text: The fourth number The number with no step is probably right. It still fails 144 late-delivery complaints from Dammam per month since July: the value Lab 2.3 also found A peer can confirm only what can be rerun. A number with no step rests on the author's word, which is what a package exists to replace. Next quarter someone updates the package: this number will silently stay 144. The repair takes five minutes: write the query, log it.

slides.title: Numbers in the text are written by the log, not typed
slides.text: Preventing drift Numbers in the text are written by the log, not typed {"name": "On-time rate on long routes", "value": 0.6805, "step": "long_short", "key": "long"} Each headline number names its step and key. The README table is generated from this file, after the last run. A number with no step cannot be entered. A change to a query changes the README in the same commit. Drift is a process problem. Nobody intends to leave an old number in a README. Remove the typing and the drift goes with it.

slides.title: The peer reruns, traces and writes. The author repairs
slides.text: How a peer works The peer reruns, traces and writes. The author repairs The peer Uses the package only, and asks nothing Reruns every logged step Traces every headline number Writes a rerun log: what matched, what did not The peer does not Fix the package quietly Pass a number because it "looks right" Rerun the request through an assistant Judge the conclusion: that is the review, a different task

slides.title: Is this package reproduced?
slides.text: Checkpoint Is this package reproduced? A peer reruns a package. Every logged step runs and gives its logged headline. The README's main number, 18.2%, appears in no step's headline; the nearest is 18.9%. What does the rerun log say? Reproduced: all steps rerun to their logged values Reproduced within tolerance: 18.2% and 18.9% are close Not reproduced: the main number does not come from any logged step Reproduced after the peer corrected the README to 18.9%

slides.text: Lab 3.3 · 25 min Rerun a supplied package Rerun a supplied package from its logs and check that the numbers match its README. D3_3_peer_rerun.ipynb Read the package's README and its log 4 min Rerun every logged step on your data 8 min Compare with the claimed numbers and trace each one 9 min Write the rerun log as the note 4 min ✱ Stretch: Write the missing step and log it so the package passes

slides.title: Disclosing assistance
slides.text: Session 4 Disclosing assistance Derive the assisted steps of an analysis from its log Write a method and disclosure paragraph that the log supports Choose a capstone question and route its tables before starting 04

slides.title: A disclosure lets the reader decide how much to rely on each part
slides.text: Disclosure A disclosure lets the reader decide how much to rely on each part Which numbers did an assistant touch? What was it shown? How was each one checked, and which were not? Who answers for them? For government entities The national guidelines ask them to be transparent about content created with generative AI. For anyone who writes code with it The guidelines for the public advise marking generated code as such, and verifying it.

slides.title: Five things, in one paragraph
slides.text: What it states Five things, in one paragraph Part The question it answers From Tool Which assistant, which model, which settings? The log Steps What did it draft or produce? The log Data seen Schema, aggregates or rows, and of what level? The data-handling table Verification How was each step checked? Which was not? The verification notes Accountability Who decided, and who signs? You Four of the five are copied from files you already have. A disclosure is hard to write only when the log does not exist.

slides.title: Two sentences, eight problems
slides.text: Lab 3.4, the draft found in the package Two sentences, eight problems The draftAI tools were used for minor formatting in this analysis. All numbers were verified by the analyst. Names no assistant and no model Names no step Does not say what the assistant saw Does not say who is accountable Calls assistance on headline numbers "minor" Claims all numbers verified: the chart step has no check The second sentence is false, and the log proves it. A disclosure that overstates verification is worse than none.

slides.title: A paragraph the log supports
slides.text: The reference paragraph A paragraph the log supports Three steps of this analysis were drafted by an AI coding assistant (rafiq-recorded-1, temperature 0.2): the quarterly on-time rate for Dammam, the comparison of long and short routes, and the weekly chart. The assistant was shown table and column names only; no rows and no personal data left the notebook. The quarterly rate was recomputed in SQL without the assistant and reconciled; the route comparison was checked with row counts, an anti-join and a stated denominator. The weekly chart was not independently verified and is illustrative. The definition of on time, the reading of the results and the recommendation are the analyst's, who is accountable for every number in this report.

slides.title: An unverified step has two honest options
slides.text: When the log shows a gap An unverified step has two honest options Verify it before the report goes out Recompute the series, read the encodings, write the note. Fifteen minutes for a chart. Say that it was not verified Name the step and say how to read it: illustrative, not a source for numbers. There is no third option. Leaving the step out of the paragraph, or folding it into "all numbers were verified", is the failure the defence looks for.

slides.title: The repository shows which code was assisted, and how
slides.text: Disclosure below the report The repository shows which code was assisted, and how In the code A header comment on an assisted query: drafted by the assistant, the log step, the check that passed. In the history Commits that separate "assistant draft" from "repair after check", so the diff is the verification. In the transcripts The conversations as they happened, including the replies that were rejected. The rejected replies are evidence in your favour. A transcript with no failed check suggests no check was run.

slides.title: Choose a question you can verify in two hours
slides.text: Tomorrow Choose a question you can verify in two hours Cash on delivery and second attempts, by city Split shifts and failed deliveries Express against standard, each on its own cut-off Complaint categories after late and after on-time parcels Replanned routes against routes planned once Failed and returned parcels by merchant segment Before you choose Which tables does it need, and where may they go? What is the one rate, and out of what? Which step will you keep? A smaller question, fully verified scores above a larger one with a headline nobody recomputed. The rubric gives verification 30 of 100.

slides.title: Which disclosure is honest?
slides.text: Checkpoint Which disclosure is honest? A log shows two assisted steps: a rate that was recomputed by hand, and a summary of complaint categories that was not checked. Which sentence belongs in the report? The rate was recomputed without the assistant; the summary was not verified and is indicative All assisted results were verified by the analyst AI assistance was used in parts of this analysis The rate was drafted by an assistant and recomputed by hand

slides.title: Leave behind what a colleague needs to stand where you stood
slides.text: Day 3 recap Leave behind what a colleague needs to stand where you stood Route first: a table takes its highest column; rows of Restricted tables never go to a hosted assistant; a guard enforces it. Log as you go: request, context, model, settings, code, data fingerprint, headline, check. Reproduced means a peer reaches the README's numbers from the package alone: matched, drifted or no step. Disclose the tool, the steps, the data seen, the verification and who signs, and say what was not verified. Delegate, verify, reproduce. The assistant drafts. You decide what it may do, prove what it did, and own what you sign.

slides.title: One question, one package, in a public repository
slides.text: What you hand over One question, one package, in a public repository Start from labs/capstone/starter and your choice from Lab 3.4. Route first: fill data_handling.md before the first request. Log as you go: every assisted step, with its transcript. Recompute each headline number without the assistant, and write its note. Five runs of one request, compared. README: numbers written from headline.json, and the disclosure paragraph. Never in the repository A key, or a row or example value of a Restricted table, in any file or transcript. Before you hand it over Run capstone/package.py check. It lists what the package still lacks.

slides.title: The rubric
slides.text: How packages are scored The rubric Brief and delegation choices 15% Verification notes 30% Variability and reproducibility 25% Data handling and disclosure 15% Findings 15% Findings are 15 of 100. A smaller question with every headline number recomputed scores above a larger one that nobody checked.

slides.title: Two hours
slides.text: Build the package Two hours Commit as you go: the history is part of the evidence. Stop analysing when forty minutes remain.

slides.title: Peer rerun · 30 minutes
slides.text: Before the first defence Peer rerun · 30 minutes Clone your colleague's repository. Run capstone/package.py rerun. Ask nothing. Commit the rerun log to their repository.

slides.title: 8 minutes for each defence, without the assistant
slides.text: Format 8 minutes for each defence, without the assistant 1 · Choices · 2 minutes The question. What you delegated, what you kept, and where the data went. 2 · Evidence · 3 minutes What verification found, which conclusion held in five runs, what your peer's rerun said. 3 · One number, live · 3 minutes The assessor chooses a headline number. You recompute it in SQL and explain any difference. Peer feedback. After each defence, everyone writes one strength, one question and one suggestion.

slides.title: What the packages showed
slides.text: Trainer review What the packages showed Strongest patterns Checks that found something, and disclosures that said what was not verified. Common gaps Numbers with no step, denominators left unstated, steps logged from memory. One surprise A conclusion that did not hold in five runs, or a null result that did.

slides.title: Keep going
slides.text: After the course Keep going The follow-up task: one assisted analysis at work or on open data, with a verification note for each headline number, sent to your trainer Your package stays yours: its layout is the template for the next analysis you sign At work: your organisation's own classification and assistant policy decide what may go where; the course's policy was written for a fictional company Next in the Academy: the other courses of the Data Science track at level 200, which lead to the DS Assistant badge
